# User stories (stage 2.4)

## Overview
Describe the requirements from the point of view of the people who use the system, so each story can be built and tested on its own.

## When to use
- `ra-aidlc phase status` shows 2.4 as current.
- Skip it, with the person's agreement, for refactors, isolated bug fixes, infrastructure or developer tooling: `ra-aidlc phase skip --stage 2.4 --reason "<why>"`.

## Process
1. `ra-aidlc stage show 2.4` and follow it.
2. Say in one line why the stage runs (or propose to skip it).
3. Questions (protocol `questions`), usually 2–4: grouping, story size, must-haves, how NFRs are handled.
4. Write `stories.md`: personas the answers support; `### US1 <title> (must)` with "As a … I want … so that … [FR-001]"; criteria `US1-AC1` with concrete values; the traceability table with every FR `covered` or `deferred`.
5. `ra-aidlc gate --stage 2.4`, then the gate.

## Common rationalizations
| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "One big story per area is simpler." | Big stories cannot be built or tested alone. Split by action. |
| "Edge cases go in the code." | Edge cases are acceptance criteria. Write the limit values. |
| "Every system needs an admin persona." | Only personas the requirements or answers support. |

## Red flags
- A story that cites no FR (invented scope).
- An FR missing from the traceability table (`traceability` fails).
- Criteria like "works correctly".

## Verification
- `ra-aidlc gate --stage 2.4` exits 0.
